notes: The BASIC text-to-video graph for the minimax-h3 catalog entry (WORKPLAN 18 P9). Fifteen core nodes and nothing else -- UNETLoader / CLIPLoader / VAELoader x2 / MiniMaxH3SigmaShift / MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo / RandomNoise / KSamplerSelect / BasicScheduler / BasicGuider / SamplerCustomAdvanced / VAEDecode / VAEDecodeAudio / CreateVideo / SaveVideo -- so it runs on the backend the panel installs with no custom packs at all and no optionalNodes machinery to fall back on. It is the AUTHORED graph's own sampling spine, read back class by class and input by input against the RUNNING managed backend's /object_info on 2026-09-09 rather than recalled: eleven of these fifteen classes are absent from scripts/comfy-node-defs.json, and the MiniMaxH3* classes in particular are comfy_extras.nodes_minimax_h3, i.e. CORE, which is easy to get backwards.
whatWasDroppedFromTheAuthoredGraph: Eleven nodes, in four groups. (1) The five model-chain patches -- ModelPreviewOverrideKJ (153), ApplyMiniMaxH3FirstBlockCache (164), MiniMaxH3MemoryEfficientSageAttentionPatch (165), MiniMaxH3ScheduledSolAttentionPatch (162) and easy cleanGpuUsed (160): every one is a pack node, and every one is a speed-or-VRAM trade rather than part of the render, so the basic wires MODEL straight from the UNETLoader through MiniMaxH3SigmaShift (core) to BasicGuider and BasicScheduler. Sigma shift is KEPT because it is core and it is model configuration, not an optimisation -- it sets the video/audio sigma schedule H3 is sampled on. (2) The size machinery -- ResolutionSelector (115) and ComfyLiterals Float (167): a megapixel float driving an aspect combo. MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo takes literal width and height (measured: INT, default 1344/768, step 32), so the basic carries the literal 1344x768 the authored graph resolved to, which is also the size the catalog's measurement was taken at. (3) The length machinery -- ComfyMathExpression (135) and PrimitiveFloat (136, 150): seconds x fps snapped to the model's 17k+5 grid. /object_info gives `length` a step of 17 and a default of 124 directly, so the basic carries a literal frame count and the fps is a literal on CreateVideo. (4) The two terminal extras -- RTXVideoSuperResolution (168), which needs the NVIDIA app video SDK and rescaled the finished frames to a fixed 1920x1080, and PlaySound|pysssss (159), a chime. Neither changes a sampled pixel; dropping the upscaler means the saved file IS the sampled 1344x768, which is the honest thing for a basic to save.
whyTheLengthIs124: 124 frames is the node's OWN declared default and the bottom of the range the model was trained on: /object_info's tooltip for MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo.length reads "Frame count at 24 fps, snapped up to the model's 17k+5 grid (124 = ~5s; trained range is ~124-362, longer is untested)". The AUTHORED graph asks for 15 s (362 frames, the top of that range), which is a >15-minute render on an RTX 5090 and was still sampling at 901 s when the catalog's own probe cancelled it (WORKPLAN 18 P3a). A basic is a proof of function, so this one is authored at the shortest length the model's author calls trained -- 124 frames, 5.17 s at 24 fps, measured at 253 s on an RTX 5090. That is a template-authoring choice and it does NOT answer WORKPLAN 18 P3a (b), which is the separate, owner-gated question of whether the PANEL should cap a duration a user asks for.

prompt.note: REQUIRED here, unlike every other basic in this bundle. H3 carries its prompt as a STRING widget on the sampler-conditioning node itself and this graph has no CLIPTextEncode at all, so the panel's generic encoder walk (comfy.js: follow KSampler.positive/negative) finds NOTHING to write to. Without this entry a generated clip would silently ignore the user's words -- the same class of silent miss as the KREA2 image that rendered as pure text-to-image.

whyNoDurationSeconds: No procedural.durationSeconds, and that is the one behavioural difference from the authored AE_LLAMA_H3_I2V_V1 manifest. That graph fed SECONDS into a ComfyMathExpression, so it had to declare durationSeconds -- which flips lengthIn to 'seconds' and makes injectParams REFUSE a frames request. This graph carries a literal numeric `length` on node 138, which is exactly what injectParams' generic frame walk writes to (comfy.js frameKeys = length/frames/video_frames/num_frames), so frames go in as frames. Same rule wan22-5b's basic follows.
whyNoResolution: No procedural.resolution. That key means 'this template derives its pixel dimensions from a MEGAPIXEL widget' (comfy.js injectProcedural), which was true of the authored graph's ResolutionSelector and is false here: node 138 takes literal width and height, which the panel injects by introspection. Declaring it would send width x height through an area conversion onto a widget that does not exist. See WORKPLAN 18 P5a for the positional-widget defect this key class produced on sd15.
whyNoFirstFrame: No procedural.firstFrame, and therefore no LoadImage node: `first_frame` is an OPTIONAL input on MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo (measured from /object_info, 2026-09-09) and omitting it IS the text-to-video path, which is what the _T2V_ in the name means. The authored graph shipped a LoadImage whose filename existed only on the owner's machine and relied on procedural.firstFrame.detachable to delete it for everyone else; a basic should not need a rescue. i2v for this entry is a SIBLING file under a new name, not a refinement of this one -- and until one exists, NO shipped template accepts a reference image at all, which is pinned in tests/test-workflow-bundle.js and filed as WORKPLAN 18 P9a.
lengthIsOnAGridOf17: H3 samples a 17k+5 frame grid and /object_info gives node 138's `length` a step of 17 (min 5, max 3600, default 124). ComfyUI does not enforce the step server-side, so a frames request off the grid is accepted and snapped by the node rather than refused. 124 frames at the CreateVideo fps of 24 is 5.17 s, which is the clip a request naming no length gets.
audioIsPartOfTheModel: The two VAELoaders and the VAEDecodeAudio are not decoration: fl2va generates video AND audio from one latent, so SamplerCustomAdvanced's single LATENT output is decoded twice -- through the video VAE for IMAGE and through the audio VAE for AUDIO -- and CreateVideo takes both. Dropping the audio half would ship a silent clip from a model whose point is that it is not silent. Verified in the field 2026-09-09: AE's own footage read of the imported mp4 reports hasAudio true.
whyNoTurboLora: The authored manifest lists an OPTIONAL 4-step turbo lora (MiniMax_H3/minimax_h3_turbo_4step_comfyui_pruned.safetensors) that its graph never loads -- there is no LoraLoader in either file. It is not listed here because this template does not use it, and a manifest that names a weight it never loads prices a download the user does not need.

customNodes.note: All fourteen classes resolve to nodes.py or comfy_extras/* on ComfyUI 0.34.0 -- verified against the running managed backend's /object_info, which reports MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo and MiniMaxH3SigmaShift as comfy_extras.nodes_minimax_h3. This template declares no optionalNodes because it needs none.

panelIntegration.promptInjection: manifest: procedural.prompt -> node 138's `prompt` widget (the generic encoder walk cannot reach it -- there is no CLIPTextEncode)
panelIntegration.saveNode: SaveVideo 92 -- mp4/h264 so AE can import it; filename_prefix is RELATIVE, so ComfyUI joins it onto its own output dir
